source_text: Quorum certe nihil a te actum est; sed postquam respondisti catholicos liberum arbitrium confiteri, de quorum te numero esse confingis, statim definitionem admovisti, quae id, quod dedisse videbaris, eriperet. Ais enim: Sed si quis ad colendum recte Deum sine ipsius adiutorio dicit esse in hominibus liberum arbitrium, hic Pelagianus vocatur; et item: Liberum arbitrium esse in hominibus dicimus, liberum autem quemquam esse ad agendum bonum vos dicitis [n129] .
pass_a_gloss: Of which certainly nothing has been done by you; but after you responded that catholics confess free choice, of whose number you invent yourself to be, you immediately moved a definition which would snatch that which you seemed to have given. For you say: But if anyone says that there is in humans free choice for worshiping God rightly without his help, this one is called Pelagian; and likewise: We say there is free choice in humans, but you say that anyone is free for doing good.

lemmas.lexica: LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS liber=free; also children; context decides

pass_b_english: You have certainly done neither. After replying that catholics acknowledge free will—and pretending to be one of them—you immediately added a definition taking away what you seemed to have granted. For you say: ‘But anyone who says humans have free will to worship God rightly without his help is called a Pelagian.’ And again: ‘We say that humans have free will; but you say that anyone is free to do good’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.8).

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
